THESE APPEALS HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT AND COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT THIS DAY THROUGH VIDEO CONFERENCING AT KALABURAGI, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

Being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 28.7.2021 passed in MVC No.557/2018 by the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge and CJM and Member, MACT, Chikkamagaluru, awarding compensation of Rs.13,23,000/- with interest 9% p.a.
from the date of petition till realization, the petitioners and the Insurance Company have approached this Court in these appeals.
The brief facts are as below:

That on 15.05.2018 at about 7.30 p.m., Sri.Suhail Ahmed (deceased) was proceeding on the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.K.A18-EF-9309 as a pillion rider, driven by one U.P.Ameer Hamza, from Uppalli to Gowrikaluve.

Near 60 feet road, Gowrikaluve, in order to avoid collision to a stray dog, the rider of the motor cycle suddenly applied the brakes resulting in the pillion rider, i.e., Suhail Ahmed to fall down on the road and sustain grievous injuries.
Then the public gathered at the spot shifted the injured to Holy-Cross Hospital, Chikkamagaluru for treatment.

Later he was shifted to Father Muller Hospital, Mangalore and then to Yenepoya Medical College Hospital,
Mangalore, where he succumbed to the said injuries on 30.05.2018.
3. The petitioners contended that, deceased Suhail Ahmed was hale and healthy, aged about aged 52 years, agriculturist and also doing labour supplier work and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.

They also contended that, the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioners No.2 and 3 are NC: 2023:KHC:41306 the children and petitioner No.4 is the mother and the petitioner No.5 is the father-in-law of deceased Suhail Ahmed and as such they are dependents of deceased.

The petitioners also alleged that, the respondent No.1 is the rider cum owner of the alleged motorcycle and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said motorcycle and insurance policy was in force as on the date of accident and as such both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

In response to the notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the Tribunal through their respective counsels and the respondent No.2 has filed the objection statement.
The respondent No.1 has not filed the objection statement.

5. The respondent No.2 contended that though the issuance of policy to offending motor bike and its validity is admitted, but the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

Further it contended that, it is learnt that at the time of accident the respondent NC:
2023:KHC:41306 No.1 was not riding the motor bike, on the other hand, deceased Suhail Ahmed was riding the motor cycle without holding valid and effective driving licence to ride the said motor cycle and as such the alleged accident has occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the deceased Suhail Ahmed.
Therefore, the claim petition filed by the petitioners is not maintainable.
The respondent No.2 also denied the age, occupation and income of the deceased as mentioned in the claim petition and termed the compensation claimed to be exorbitant and imaginary.

6. In view of above contentions raised, the Tribunal framed following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that husband of the 1st petitioner, father of petitioners No.2, 3 and son of petitioner NO.4 and 5 by name Suhail Ahamed died in the hospital on 30.05.2018 at 12.00 PM, due to the grievous injuries sustained by him on 15.05.2018 at about 7.30 PM, in front of mutton shop, on 60 feet road,
Gowrikaluve, Chikkamagaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA:
18/EF:9309 as averred in the petition?
2.
Whether the respondent No.2 proves that the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-18/EF-9309 had no driving NC: 2023:KHC:41306 licence as on the date of accident?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitle for compensation?
If yes, for what amount and from whom?
4. What order or award?

ADDL. ISSUE 1. Whether the respondent No.2 proves that deceased Suhail himself was riding the motor cycle and he had no driving licence and accident was occurred due to his own negligence as averred in the objection?
7.
The petitioner No.1 was examined as PW1 and Exs.
P1 to P12 were marked in the evidence.
Respondent No.2 Insurance Company examined its officials as RWs 1 and 2 and a witness as RW3 and Exs.R1 to R4 were marked.
RW1 did not appear for cross-examination and as such, his evidence was discarded.
Respondent No.1 was examined as RW4 and Exs.R5 and 6 were marked.

After hearing the arguments by both the sides, the Tribunal answered issue No. 1 in the affirmative, issue No.2 and additional Issue No.1 in the negative and issue No.3 partly in the affirmative and passed the impugned judgment fastening liability on the Insurance Company and by NC: 2023:KHC:41306 awarding a sum of Rs.13,23,000/- under different heads as below:
Towards loss of dependency Rs.10,89,000/-
Towards loss of estate Rs. 15,000/-

Towards transportation of dead body and Rs. 15,000/- funeral expenses Towards medical expenses Rs. 84,000/- Towards parental consortium Rs. 80,000/-

Being aggrieved by the said judgment, the petitioner Nos. 1 to 5 have approached this Court in MFA No.5408/2021 contending that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is meager and on the lower side and the quantum of compensation be reassessed by this court.

10. Being aggrieved by the said judgment the insurance Company has come up in appeal in MFA No.5391/2021 contending that the deceased Suhail Ahmed was riding the motor cycle which met with the accident and this fact was not properly appreciated by the Tribunal.
The Tribunal should have dismissed the petition as against the - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:41306 Insurance Company, but by improperly appreciating the evidence, it has passed the impugned award.
11. In MFA No.5408/2021, notice to respondent No.1 was served and unrepresented and respondent No.2- Insurance Company appeared through its counsel before this Court.
In MFA No.5391/2021 the petitioners/ respondents No.1 to 4 and respondent No. 6 have appeared through their counsels and service of notice against respondent No.5 is held sufficient.
12. On admission, the Tribunal records have been secured and the arguments by both the sides were heard.

13. The learned counsel Sri Lakshminarasappa for Sri A.M. Venkatesh appearing for the Insurance Company submits that the MLC Register extract of Holy Cross Hospital, Chikkamagaluru, which is produced by the Insurance Company at Ex.R2 clearly show that the deceased Suhail Ahmed was riding the motor cycle and he fell down due to a skid and then he was hit by another motor cycle M/S National Insurance Co. He further contended that it was a self accident and therefore, the Insurance Company be absolved from the liability.

In support of his contention, he has relied upon the decision in the case of Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Limited Vs. B.C. Kumar and another1 and in the case of Veerappa and another Vs.

Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners contended that the Insurance Company has not proved the Ex.R2 by examining its author and the contents of Ex.R2 were not put across to the RW4, who in fact, admitted that he was the rider of the motor cycle at the time of the accident.

Therefore, he contends that the ILR 2009 Karnataka 2921 ILR 2009 Karnataka 3562 (2009) 15 SCC 165 - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:41306 contents of Ex.R2 that the deceased Suhail Ahmed was riding the motor cycle are not proved by the Insurance Company.

sentences.text: But on the other hand, the entire investigation papers of the police are corroborated by none else than the respondent No.1 and as such, the Tribunal was right in fastening liability on the Insurance Company.
He further contends that the notional income of the deceased was not properly considered by the Tribunal and therefore, a reassessment of the compensation is necessary.

15. In these appeals the questions that arise are;
A. Whether the deceased was the rider of the motor cycle or it was the respondent No.1? and B.
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded is just and reasonable?
16.

The decision in the case of NWKRTC Vs. Gourabai and others referred supra relied by the Insurance Company lays down that when the Medical Officer had stated before the Tribunal that the injury caused was due to fall from the height of 8 to 10 feet and the same was mentioned in the hospital records, it was established that - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:41306 there was no involvement of a vehicle.
Therefore, the Insurance Company was absolved from liability.

B.C.Kumar and another referred supra lays down that the Tribunal should not and ought not to place the reliance on the judgment of the Criminal Court while considering the issue of factum of the accident and the subsequent negligence.

sentences.text: But it has to assess the evidence independently of any finding of the Criminal Court on the question of driver pleading guilty.

18. The decision in the case of Veerappa and another Vs. Siddappa and another referred supra rendered by a Division Bench of this Court holds that even though the owner of the vehicle in unmistakable terms has admitted the accident, the admission has no value in the eye of law.

sentences.text: It was observed that though the accident occurred on 26-6- 2001 and the injured died on 28-6-2001, no complaint was lodged till 28-8-2001.
It was also observed that the police earlier had filed a chargesheet against the deceased himself - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:41306 and therefore, it was supressed and it was a clear case of fraud.
19. Obviously, the above cases can very well be distinguished on facts.
In the case on hand, none of the medical officer, who was responsible for the entries in medico legal register is examined.
Moreover, the source of information in Ex.R2 is not established.
The the evidence available on record shows that except Ex.R2, there is nothing to show that the deceased was riding the motor cycle.
20. A perusal of Ex.R2 would show that it was none else than the RW4/respondent No.1 Ameer, who had taken the deceased to Holy cross hospital.
Ex . R2
contain his phone number also.
It was noted in Ex.R2 as below:

"A/M/D RTA at around 7.30 p.m. near Kadur road H/O cycle skid and rider (Mr.
Suhil) and pillion Ameer fell off cycle............ Pt.53 years old male while riding cycle skid and fell at around 7.30 p.m. and was hit by another motor cycle while on the road.
A/H/O 2nd cycle going over chest of Mr. Suhil, details of second cycler unavailable....."
Ex.R2 does not contain the name of the Medical Officer who wrote Ex.R2.
But however, the official of the Insurance company examined as RW2 states in his cross- examination that the concerned Medical Officer is Dr. Sukesh Geralda.

The perusal of the evidence of RW3, the private investigator of the Insurance Company shows that he only obtained certain documents from the hospital and he has submitted a detailed report to the Insurance Company.
However, though Ex.R3 is the document issued by him, the said document was not marked through him or shown to him.

It is to be noted that nowhere RW3 or the Ex.R3 show that it was Dr. Sukesh Geralda who had written M/S National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Mrs Ifshan Ara on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28788794/
8 the Ex.R2.

sentences.text: Obviously, Dr. Sukesh Geralda is not examined by the Insurance Company.
Another copy of Ex.R2 is also available at Ex.R4.
In the said document also, there is no mention of Dr. Sukesh Geralda.
22. The respondent No.1 - Ameer is examined as RW4.

Though he initially deny the negligence on his part, he admits that in order to avoid the hitting of dog he applied - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:41306 brakes and the deceased, who was the pillion rider, fell down on the road.
In his cross-examination by the learned counsel for the Insurance Company it is elicited that he had sustained minor injuries and he had not claimed any insurance or the damages to the vehicle.
He has denied that deceased Suhail was riding the motor cycle.
It is pertinent to note that there is no suggestion to him that he had furnished the information to the Medical Officer of Holy Cross hospital to make the necessary entries as mentioned in Ex.R2.
As noted supra, Ex.R2 MLC Register extract show that the deceased Suhail was brought by Ameer.
Therefore, it is evident that the source of the information for narrating the incident in Ex.R2 is not available or established.

23. On the contrary, the petitioners, came to know about the accident later from the rider of the motor cycle and some public and a relative of the deceased Suhail has lodged complaint to the police as per Ex.P1.
Ex . P1 which was lodged on the very next day of the accident show that Ameer was the rider and the deceased Suhail was the pillion - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC:41306 rider.
It is also mentioned in the complaint that since the deceased had to be shifted to Father Muller's hospital, Mangalore, for higher treatment, he could not lodge the complaint on the same day.
This explanation also appears to be acceptable.
24. The Investigating Officer, investigated the matter and ultimately filed the chargesheet against the said Ameer as per Ex.P7.
Therefore, an investigation by a Police Officer stands on a higher footing than the investigation made by a private investigator like RW3.
There is no effort made by the Insurance Company by summoning the Police Officer, who investigated the matter and confront him with MLC records and the investigation report of RW3.

Therefore, the available evidence show that except Ex.R2, which do not get corroboration from any corners, there is nothing on record to show that it was the deceased Suhail who was riding the motor cycle and Ameer was the pillion rider.

All other evidence i.e., the FIR, chargesheet, and such other investigation papers, the testimony of RW4 show that - 18 - NC: 2023:KHC:41306 deceased Suhail was the pillion rider of the motor cycle and it was driven by Ameer.
Under these circumstances, the Rule of preponderance of probability lies in favour of the petitioners.

Thought Ex.R2- MLC Register Extract creates some doubt, it is not enough to rebut and M/S National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Mrs Ifshan Ara on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28788794/
9 overcome the probability of evidence available on record.

sentences.text: Therefore, when there is no delay in filing the FIR, when the source of the information for the entries in the MLC extract is not available, when the police investigation remain unchallenged and when the private investigator do not ascertain and disclose his source of information, it has to be held that the version of the petitioners which is supported by the chargesheet holds the field.
This Court is unable to accede to the contentions of the Insurance Company that deceased himself was the rider of the motor cycle.

25. The Tribunal in para 22 to 25 and in para 32 has discussed the available evidence on record and has come to the conclusion that it was the respondent No.1 Ameer, who was the owner of the motor cycle was the rider at the time - 19 - NC: 2023:KHC:41306 of the accident.
In no way, the said findings can be termed to be perverse or arbitrary.

Moreover, when the Tribunal has formed an opinion based on the evidence recorded by it,
unless such conclusion is perverse and arbitrary, the appellate court cannot replace such conclusions by its own.
26. The second question that arises is regarding the quantum.

The learned counsel for the petitioners contended that the Tribunal erred in appreciating the fact that Ex.P12 show that the deceased was an agriculturist and therefore, his income should have been properly assessed by it.
A perusal of Ex.P12 shows that it is an RTC pertaining to the year 1976-77 and the property stands in the name of one Fateh Mohammed.
Obviously, it is for the year 1976-1977 and the current RTC is not available.
Therefore, the Tribunal was right in holding that notional income has to be adopted.
The Tribunal considers the notional income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month.
The accident has occurred in the year 2018.
The guidelines issued by KSLSA for settlement of disputes before the Lok Adalath prescribe a notional - 20 - NC: 2023:KHC:41306 income of Rs.12,500/- per month for the year 2018.
In umpteen numbers of decisions, this Court has held that the guidelines prescribed by KSLSA are in general conformity with the wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act.
Therefore, the notional income of the deceased has to be considered at Rs.12,500/- per month.
27. The deceased was aged about 53 years at the time of the accident and therefore, the future prospects at 10% is to be added to the notional income and the appropriate multiplier would be 11.

Hence, the loss of dependency is calculated as: Rs.13,750/-(12,500/- +1,250/-) x 12 x  x 11=
Rs.13,61,250/- by deducting 1/4th towards the personal expenses of the deceased.

28. In addition to the above compensation, the petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rs.48,400/-
towards loss of consortium, Rs.18,150/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses.

Though the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.80,000/- towards parental consortium, in view of the decision in the case of Shri Ram General Insurance M/S National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Mrs Ifshan Ara on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28788794/

sentences.text: However, a sum of Rs.84,000/- awarded by the Tribunal towards medical expenses do not call for interference.

Therefore, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under different heads as below:
Towards loss of dependency Rs.13,61,250/- Towards loss of consortium Rs. 48,400/-
Towards loss of estate Rs. 18,150/-
Towards funeral expenses Rs. 18,150/-
Towards medical expenses Rs. 84,000/-

Less: awarded by the Tribunal Rs.13,23,000/-
Enhancement Rs. 2,06,950/-
Thus, the petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rs.2,06,950/- in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal together with interest.
In the result, the appeal filed by the petitioners deserves to be allowed in part and the appeal filed by the Insurance Company deserves to be dismissed.

Hence, the following:
Civil Appeal No.2410/2023 DD 27-3-2023 - 22 - NC: 2023:KHC:41306 ORDER (i) The appeal filed by the petitioners in MFA No.5408/2021 is allowed in part.
(ii) The appeal filed by the Insurance Company in MFA No.5391/2021 is dismissed.

(iii) The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified by awarding a sum of Rs.2,06,950/- in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% p.a from the date of petition till its deposit.
(iv) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the same within four weeks before the Tribunal.
(v) The rest of the order passed by the tribunal remains unaltered.
(vi) The amount in deposit, if any, in MFA No.5391/2021 shall be transmitted to the jurisdictional Tribunal forthwith.

M/S National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Mrs Ifshan Ara on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28788794/
But it has to assess the evidence independently of any finding of the Criminal Court on the question of driver pleading guilty.
Therefore, an investigation by a Police Officer stands on a higher footing than the investigation made by a private investigator like RW3.
There is no effort made by the Insurance Company by summoning the Police Officer, who investigated the matter and confront him with MLC records and the investigation report of RW3.
Therefore, the available evidence show that except Ex.R2, which do not get corroboration from any corners, there is nothing on record to show that it was the deceased Suhail who was riding the motor cycle and Ameer was the pillion rider.
Under these circumstances, the Rule of preponderance of probability lies in favour of the petitioners.
Therefore, when there is no delay in filing the FIR, when the source of the information for the entries in the MLC extract is not available, when the police investigation remain unchallenged and when the private investigator do not ascertain and disclose his source of information, it has to be held that the version of the petitioners which is supported by the chargesheet holds the field.
This Court is unable to accede to the contentions of the Insurance Company that deceased himself was the rider of the motor cycle.
In no way, the said findings can be termed to be perverse or arbitrary.
Moreover, when the Tribunal has formed an opinion based on the evidence recorded by it,
unless such conclusion is perverse and arbitrary, the appellate court cannot replace such conclusions by its own.
The learned counsel for the petitioners contended that the Tribunal erred in appreciating the fact that Ex.P12 show that the deceased was an agriculturist and therefore, his income should have been properly assessed by it.
A perusal of Ex.P12 shows that it is an RTC pertaining to the year 1976-77 and the property stands in the name of one Fateh Mohammed.
Therefore, the Tribunal was right in holding that notional income has to be adopted.
The accident has occurred in the year 2018.
In umpteen numbers of decisions, this Court has held that the guidelines prescribed by KSLSA are in general conformity with the wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act.
opennyai_summary.decision:
The Tribunal considers the notional income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month.
The guidelines issued by KSLSA for settlement of disputes before the Lok Adalath prescribe a notional - 20 - NC: 2023:KHC:41306 income of Rs.12,500/- per month for the year 2018.
Therefore, the notional income of the deceased has to be considered at Rs.12,500/- per month.
27. The deceased was aged about 53 years at the time of the accident and therefore, the future prospects at 10% is to be added to the notional income and the appropriate multiplier would be 11.
Hence, the loss of dependency is calculated as: Rs.13,750/-(12,500/- +1,250/-) x 12 x  x 11=
Rs.13,61,250/- by deducting 1/4th towards the personal expenses of the deceased.
28. In addition to the above compensation, the petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rs.48,400/-
towards loss of consortium, Rs.18,150/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses.
Though the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.80,000/- towards parental consortium, in view of the decision in the case of Shri Ram General Insurance M/S National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Mrs Ifshan Ara on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28788794/
10 - 21 - NC: 2023:KHC:41306
Company Limited Vs. Bhagat Singh Rawat and others4 there shall be a cap of Rs.40,000/- only in respect of the consortium.
However, a sum of Rs.84,000/- awarded by the Tribunal towards medical expenses do not call for interference.
Therefore, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under different heads as below:
Towards loss of dependency Rs.13,61,250/- Towards loss of consortium Rs. 48,400/-
Towards loss of estate Rs. 18,150/-
Towards funeral expenses Rs. 18,150/-
Towards medical expenses Rs. 84,000/-
Total Rs.15,29,950/-
Less: awarded by the Tribunal Rs.13,23,000/-
Enhancement Rs. 2,06,950/-
Thus, the petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rs.2,06,950/- in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal together with interest.
In the result, the appeal filed by the petitioners deserves to be allowed in part and the appeal filed by the Insurance Company deserves to be dismissed.
Hence, the following:
Civil Appeal No.2410/2023 DD 27-3-2023 - 22 - NC: 2023:KHC:41306 ORDER (i) The appeal filed by the petitioners in MFA No.5408/2021 is allowed in part.
(ii) The appeal filed by the Insurance Company in MFA No.5391/2021 is dismissed.
(iii) The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified by awarding a sum of Rs.2,06,950/- in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% p.a from the date of petition till its deposit.
(iv) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the same within four weeks before the Tribunal.
(v) The rest of the order passed by the tribunal remains unaltered.
(vi) The amount in deposit, if any, in MFA No.5391/2021 shall be transmitted to the jurisdictional Tribunal forthwith.
In view of the disposal of the main matters, the pending IAs, if any, are also disposed of.
